articles.title: ‘You don’t wanna get burned’: As Patrick Mahomes, Bo Nix return, NFL defensive minds split on how to game-plan for QBs in first game back from injury

articles.body:
When the NFL released its season schedule in May, the league's calculated risk flashed.

In a vacuum, scheduling the Denver Broncos to face the Kansas City Chiefs for the "Monday Night Football" season opener made perfect sense. Two competitive teams with star quarterbacks and Super Bowl-winning coaches playing a division game? The intrigue was obvious.

But zoom out, and zoom back to May: The schedule-makers were banking on answers yet undelivered. The Chiefs' quarterback, two-time MVP Patrick Mahomes , was still rehabilitating from tearing his left ACL and LCL on Dec. 14. The Broncos ' quarterback, Bo Nix , had undergone one surgery after a Jan. 17 ankle fracture and another in April to clean up bone spurs.

Neither injury seemed likely to threaten the quarterbacks' careers. But starting Week 1? Back in May, banking on that was more optimistic than certain.

Fast forward to now, and both Nix and Mahomes are on track to start Monday night after fully participating in their respective training camps. Nix dissolved concerns about his limitations early in camp when throwing a 48-yard pass on the run, Broncos head coach Sean Payton told Yahoo Sports . Nix also played in the preseason.

Mahomes did not play in the preseason, as he had in seven prior pro campaigns, but he's scheduled to start on Monday.

"Pretty good chance that Patrick will go ahead and start unless something were to come up here in the next couple days," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters on Tuesday. "But most likely, he'll be the guy that's out there."

Reid added that Mahomes has "shown everything" in preseason work, running and throwing as normal albeit with the addition of a knee brace.

So as two teams whom oddsmakers expect to produce winning seasons face off, how much will and should the Chiefs and Broncos defenses factor the quarterbacks' injuries into their game plans?

Yahoo Sports surveyed 17 sources from 11 NFL teams during training camp to find out. The sources include one head coach, six defensive coordinators, one defensive assistant coach and nine players. Four of the nine players are edge rushers, four are defensive backs and one plays linebacker.

Several see the merit in both arguments. A narrow 9-8 majority argued the risk of factoring injuries into game plans outweighs the reward. The eight-person minority advocated that at least some game plan or playbook tweaks could deliver valuable edges.

"I don't necessarily think that you want to overreact either way the first game of the season … " Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said. "Try to see where they're at, whether it's press them more from a different side or sitting back and seeing if they're gonna run around. You might take some liberties when it comes to that.

"But you don't wanna get burned the hard way when they're healthier than you think."

The cases for, against defenses trying to capitalize on QB injury

Broncos veteran edge rusher Zach Allen has watched quarterbacks seem to defy the laws of biology and physics.

Allen played then-Seattle Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson in 2021 during Wilson's second game back from surgery to repair a ruptured tendon and fracture-dislocation in his middle finger, Wilson throwing for 207 yards against Allen's Arizona Cardinals and posting a four-touchdown game later that season. Allen has watched more recently as injuries have limited Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow in three of six pro seasons. Repeatedly, Burrow has returned on a heater. (Think: two four-touchdown games in his first four back from a turf toe surgery last season.)

"The quarterback play is at probably the highest level it's ever been," says Allen, who will start against Mahomes on Monday. "When they come back, it's kind of like they're back at full strength. If anything, they're rested and feel better."

Accelerating rehabilitation timelines leaves some defensive opponents wary of underestimating players' physical resilience. Others cite the psychological element of rehabilitation for athletes disciplined enough to thrive professionally. That "innate competitor" trait that helped them reach these professional heights can't be understated, Seattle Seahawks defensive coordinator Aden Durde said.

Cowboys defensive pass game coordinator Derrick Ansley broke down his tactical expectation for Mahomes and Nix.

"Most of these guys are going to play on-platform anyway," said Ansley, who also coaches Cowboys defensive backs. "Pat's always been quicker than fast, so he's still going to have that instinct. Same thing with Bo. There's no real advantage. …

"My opinion: Just scout it straight up and start with what they do well from past film."

Eight of the coaches and players believed injury layoffs create opportunity.

San Francisco defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who has also prepared for opponents as a head coach, said the psychology of injury warrants game-plan shifts. Making contact with the quarterback early — legally, of course — could create discomfort. Facing a quarterback who hasn't played in the preseason raises the stakes for initial live contact.

"Quarterbacks, particularly when they're coming off injury … want to go back to their roots," Morris said. "And when they go back to their roots, you want to be able to find those things and try to exploit things as quick as you can on defense."

Defenders and coaches cited movement as a key cue they'd look for in facing Mahomes or Nix in Week 1. Is the quarterback moving more fluidly to his left or the right? If one looks weaker, try to force them in that direction. Does the quarterback move outside the pocket by choice? Some surveyed voted to sit back and test the quarterback's appetite for movement, while others advocated instead for pushing the pocket early.

"Different people give off different keys, so you just want to read your keys," Seahawks edge rusher DeMarcus Lawrence said. "Is it hard for them to step up in the pocket or [do] they like to roll out? Patrick Mahomes likes to move around and stuff. So, OK, is his ACL limiting him from rolling out to his right versus his left? … OK, he had an ACL surgery: So when, it's a pass, [are] his legs straight versus bent? Or is he up on his toes?"

Defensive backs surveyed were eager to join their front-seven teammates in creating pressure on a quarterback. Steelers safety DeShon Elliott compared facing a quarterback returning from injury to facing a rookie quarterback in the NFL. There are questions they've yet to answer and rust they've yet to knock off — behold, opportunity.

"Blitz they ass," Elliott said. "Get after they ass because that'll be the first chance having live bullets. You can simulate that all you want, but that's not football. You can't touch the quarterback at practice. So you get after that ass and you blitz. Send it. You send it because it might give them a little jitters.

"And then once they get the jitters, it could be wraps."

What tells will Broncos, Chiefs look for in their chess match?

Expect each defense to test quarterbacks early in the game. But just because a test hasn't come by, say, halftime, doesn't mean it won't come later.

"If you can have that little extra waiting that he hasn't seen, I think that's important for guys like that," said Indianapolis Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo, who coordinated the 2021 Bengals defense that beat Mahomes in the AFC championship game. "You got to try to save a little something so [they think], 'Hey, they don't have that today.' And then maybe you do. It's something that they're not ready for."

In between those early tests and the later ones, each defense must heed not only the opposing quarterback's health but also the shifting pieces around him.

The Broncos enter this season with a remarkably consistent roster from last year but change in two key offensive areas: play-caller and receiver. First-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb has taken over play-calling duties from Payton, a move expected to bring more shifts and motions, different run-pass option concepts and varied use of tempo at the line of scrimmage. The Broncos also traded their 2026 first-round draft pick (and swapped late-round picks) for speedy receiver Jaylen Waddle , who will challenge a Chiefs defense that lost its starting cornerbacks to the Los Angeles Rams this spring.

Nix nonetheless expects Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo to vary coverages.

"I feel like he's going to have many bags of tricks and have a lot thrown at us, but at least I can see it a little bit," Nix said of entering his fifth career game vs. the Chiefs. "I've seen a lot of their structure and I've gotten more and more comfortable. …

"He'll throw a lot of different things at you and make you respond. We're going to be ready for it but also have to adjust."

Kansas City , meanwhile, has added Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III to stabilize its run game after falling to 20th in yards per game last season, the lowest production in Mahomes' starting era. Wide receiver Rashee Rice has returned from injury as an outlet in the passing game. But Mahomes is returning behind a compromised offensive line that's promoted undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle in place of 2025 first-round pick Josh Simmons (back) . If Mahomes favors his right side on movement, that could say more about the offensive line than the strength of his left knee.

He will wear his knee brace for the game, Mahomes said Wednesday.

"I mean, it was kind of designed for my type of injury," Mahomes said. "I'm very comfortable with it and that's why I've practiced throughout OTAs and training camp and then now, being in the season, is to kind of prepare myself to be comfortable with it. I don't even think about it when I have it on other than when it gets loose. Usually it's better when I wear pants, so I'm excited for that.

"Maybe I'll have to slide a little differently, but other than that, I'll be able to go out there and play."

Nix and Mahomes both will be able to go out there to play, validating the NFL schedule-makers' May decision to stage this game in a standalone prime-time window.

NFL fans will be watching Nix's ankle and Mahomes' knee closely. Chiefs and Broncos defenders, too, will be on alert for any tells.

"Obviously I want to test him and see if he's still Patrick and if he's moving like Patrick because the best thing he did was play off schedule," Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph said. "That's always our calling card is to make quarterbacks move off the spot and make them run for their lives. So we'll see if he can do that. But nothing different.

"I wouldn't pressure him more often than not because sometimes, when you pressure a veteran quarterback, it makes it easy for him. …

"Nothing really schematically different, but obviously [got] to get him off his mark and see if he's Patrick."

Jori Epstein is a senior NFL reporter for Yahoo Sports and the author of 'The Upstander: How Surviving the Holocaust Sparked Max Glauben's Mission to Dismantle Hate.' She previously reported for USA TODAY and The Dallas Morning News. Follow Jori on Twitter @JoriEpstein.

articles.title: NFL Narrowly Misses Making History with High-Scoring Week 1 After Mahomes, Chiefs Beat Nix, Broncos
articles.summary: NFL offenses came out hot in the 2026 season and just missed the record for the highest Week 1 scoring average since the AFL and NFL merged in 1970.
articles.body:
NFL offenses came out hot in the 2026 season and just missed the record for the highest Week 1 scoring average since the AFL and NFL merged in 1970.

According to The Athletic's Jayna Bardahl , "Entering Monday's Week 1 capper between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs, teams have scored 750 points, for an average of 50.0 points per game. According to the NFL, if that average holds, it would surpass the 49.4 points per game scored in Week 1 in 2012. That week featured a total of 791 points, so the Broncos and Chiefs need a combined 42 points to set the record."

The Broncos and Chiefs fell just short of that total with 41 points, as Patrick Mahomes and Co. defeated Bo Nix's squad 31-10.

As for the Week 1 offensive onslaught, Ben Johnson's Chicago Bears led the way, beating the Carolina Panthers 59-37. Chicago had a whopping 552 yards of total offense (and the Panthers weren't far behind with 478). Fireworks were not in short supply.

In total, 11 of the 30 teams who played scored 30 or more points, while half of the league's teams put up 25 or more points. Four games featured both teams in action scoring 25 or more points.

It was the type of week that fantasy football enthusiasts love, defensive purists hate and probably requires a whole lot of recovery sleep for NFL RedZone host Scott Hanson.

But it still fell just short of the record.

articles.title: Chargers suddenly face must-win game Week 2 vs. Raiders, with a brutal schedule after that
articles.summary: The Chargers laid an egg in Week 1 against the Cardinals, and their schedule is about to get much tougher. That's why they can't start 0-2.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers suddenly don't have a lot of wiggle room. When the schedules were announced this spring, it appeared that they had a two-game buffer — home contests against the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders — to help prepare them for the meatiest part of their slate.

Then the Chargers laid an egg in the opener against an Arizona team predicted to be in full rebuild mode. Nothing went right — offense, defense or special teams. Now the Chargers' margin for error has evaporated.

Is the Week 2 game against the Raiders a must-win? It sure feels that way.

Yes, 0-2 teams make the playoffs. But since the league went to the 17-game schedule in 2021, only eight of the 40 teams that started 0-2 ended up making it to the playoffs. That's higher than the playoff rate during the 16-game era, but not by much.

The stakes will rise significantly after Week 2. The Chargers will have to go on the road to face the Bills and Seahawks in Weeks 3 and 4, then they're home against the Broncos in Week 5, followed by a road trip to Kansas City ahead of the Week 7 bye.

That's a murderers' row. Going 0-2 and trying to make the postseason after that gauntlet just doesn't feel feasible.

Determining a team's fate after Week 1 is risky business. The two Super Bowl teams from a season ago, the Patriots and Seahawks, both lost at home in their first games. Fluky games happen.

But the Chargers' struggles ran deep Sunday, and they affected all three units. Is there hope they can pull out of this early tailspin?

Let's start with the offense. After the opening-drive TD, it never got on schedule. All preseason long, it was hard to find a bad word spoken about Mike McDaniel and the endless possibilities with a quarterback of Justin Herbert 's caliber, along with a tuned-up offensive line and a host of weapons.

We saw virtually none of that Sunday. Against a defense that was near the bottom of every major category statistically a year ago.

The Chargers were 2 for 8 on third downs against the Cardinals, plus a surprising 0 for 3 on fourth downs. Jim Harbaugh isn't the least-aggressive coach on fourth downs, but he's far from the most, which is why it was surprising to see him not try to tie the game on the first fourth-down failure, trailing only 10-7 late in the second quarter.

Perhaps Harbaugh could sense that his offense would be up against it when he made that slightly uncharacteristic decision. They crossed midfield only once after halftime, and that was with good starting field position at their own 40-yard line.

The run game was unimpressive. The Chargers were wholly undisciplined, from pass protection to Herbert's accuracy to penalties. There was a six-snap stretch in the fourth quarter, with the desperate Chargers down 23-14 with less than five minutes to go, where they were flagged four times — including on their fourth-down stop.

If we count the fourth-down failures, the Chargers turned the ball over five times and had a punt blocked deep in their own zone in 10 possessions. That's absurdly bad efficiency. And to make matters worse, Ladd McConkey , who was probably their best offensive player Sunday, suffered a chest injury.

Defensively, they were a mess, too. They allowed nearly 400 yards and were on the field nearly 38 minutes — including most of the first half. They couldn't get off the field and lost the field-possession battle early and often.

"There were quite a few things," Harbaugh said. "Much to get better at. … It's not the start that we wanted, but credit to the Cardinals. And it'll be about our resolve, our way we bounce back."

Division games always matter a little more, but the Chargers' circumstances make Sunday's game at SoFi Stadium even more important.

The Raiders started their season with a solid Week 1 win, but then again, they beat the Patriots in New England in the first game a year ago and won only twice more all season. Even still, there were some pretty encouraging moments from Las Vegas against the Dolphins.

The offensive line appeared to be solid to good in coach Klint Kubiak's debut. Kirk Cousins had mostly clean pockets, and the run game was mostly productive. The passing game felt tame at times without Brock Bowers , and Cousins threw two picks, but there were some encouraging signs.

The Raiders' defense, led by a rejuvenated Maxx Crosby , started well and finished strong. They allowed Miami only 108 yards after halftime, forcing empty possessions on six of Miami's seven second-half possessions.

The Chargers might have owned the Raiders by double-digit points in both matchups a season ago, but this feels like it'll be a tougher challenge Sunday. Especially if Bowers can return, which apparently remains a possibility.

Even with Bowers, the Raiders might not have quite the skill-position talent the Cardinals do, but they're not far off. And the Kubiak formula is similar: They can chew some clock, as they did vs. Miami, for the first three quarters anyway. The Chargers know they have to get off the field on third downs.

Offensively, the Chargers must be better on first downs. They also have to protect far better, especially against Crosby, who had a two-sack game against them late last season and who had 1.5 sacks and seven pressures on Sunday. The Raiders reduced his snap count somewhat in Week 1, compared to years past, and the strategy appeared to pay off.

McDaniel has to find a way to get the run game cooking as a way to open up the playbook and keep those pass rushers at bay. The Raiders really honed in on De'Von Achane in Week 1, and they held him to 36 yards rushing on 11 carries, with a long run of 10. That likely can't be what Omarion Hampton 's Week 2 stat line looks like if the Chargers want to get things going.

The Chargers still have strong talent, especially on offense, but what we saw in Week 1 was discouraging. McDaniel's system might still need some time to marinate, but time appears to be the one thing they're really short on right now.

articles.title: “It just took a lot out of me": Gisele Bündchen opens up about severe panic attacks and the life lessons she learned after Tom Brady divorce
articles.summary: NFL News: Gisele Bündchen has spent much of her life in the public eye, but some of her hardest battles happened away from the cameras. The former supermodel ha.
articles.body: Gisele Bündchen has spent much of her life in the public eye, but some of her hardest battles happened away from the cameras. The former supermodel has opened up about the panic attacks she faced in her early 20s, describing the experience as a turning point that changed how she viewed her body, choices and future. Years later, after her marriage to Tom Brady ended, those lessons continued to shape the way she approached life and wellness.Gisele Bündchen reveals how panic attacks changed her lifeBündchen entered modelling as a teenager and quickly found herself living at a pace few people could sustain. Success brought travel, work and global attention, but the pressure also took a toll.By her early 20s, she was dealing with severe panic attacks for around two years. Instead of simply trying to push through them, Bündchen eventually began looking at what was happening beneath the surface.She recently reflected on that period during an appearance on the i-D podcast. Her description was not simply about anxiety. It was about losing touch with herself and then slowly finding her way back.“I feel like there is many deaths and rebirths in my life,” she shared on the i-D podcast, answering a fan's question. “I think when you're 46, you definitely have gone through a few of those, but I would say one of the most intense ones for me was when I had panic attacks, and I was dealing with it in my early 20s for about two years. I think I was living so much outside of myself, almost detached and trying to be a pleaser.“It's when I really had to dive deep, and I discovered who I was, and I realized that my body was my temple and I could be the director of my own movie, that I could create my life, and that was very powerful moment. So I'm very grateful. That's why I say, ‘What doesn't kill you makes you stronger.'”That period became a foundation for Bündchen's approach to wellness. She later made changes to her diet and daily habits, placing greater importance on health rather than simply maintaining the image expected of her.Gisele Bündchen and Tom Brady faced a life-changing splitBündchen's personal journey took another major turn through her marriage to Tom Brady. The couple married in 2009 and became parents to Benjamin and Vivian. Their relationship brought family life into an already demanding world of professional sports and modelling.Their divorce in 2022 marked another difficult transition. Brady later acknowledged how deeply the separation affected him, including its impact on his football career.“It was a challenge,” Brady told FOX News. “It just took a lot out of me in terms of my ability to continue to play.”Bündchen also spoke about the emotional weight of seeing a future she had imagined take a different path.“It's tough because you imagine your life was going to be a certain way, and you did everything you could, you know?” she told Vanity Fair.Rather than allowing those experiences to define her, Bündchen continued building a life around health and self-awareness. Her 2024 book, Nourish, further explored those ideas and encouraged readers to think differently about their relationship with food and wellbeing.“This is my temple,” Bündchen said on GMA. “I only get one, so I how can I nourish it? And how can I love it? If it's not nourishing me, then I'm not going to eat it. I think that's the number one thing. Making a commitment to your health.”For Bündchen, the biggest lesson from those difficult chapters appears to be ownership. Fame, marriage and major life changes brought challenges she could not always control. But she found a way to regain control over how she cared for herself and what came next.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chiefs-Broncos Inactives: Garrett Nussmeier named emergency quarterback
articles.summary: Kansas City and Denver have released their inactive player lists for Monday’s game.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have released their list of inactive players for the season opener of "Monday Night Football" against the Denver Broncos .

The Chiefs will play without safety Chamarri Conner (knee), offensive tackles Josh Simmons (back) and Diego Pounds, defensive tackle Bryson Eason, tight end Jared Wiley and defensive end Jack Pyburn. Rookie Garrett Nussmeier has been designated as Kansas City's emergency quarterback — meaning he is only eligible to enter the game should both starter Patrick Mahomes and backup Justin Fields leave with injuries.

This appears to be the first time Kansas City has named an emergency quarterback since the rule was created in 2023.

Kansas City had already ruled Conner and Simmons out on the final injury report. Defensive tackle Chris Jones was held out of the team's final practice with a calf issue, but he was not given an injury game status. As expected, Jones is active for the contest.

On Monday, Kansas City elevated practice squad defensive tackle Marcus Harris and fullback Ben VanSumeren to the active roster. As elevated players, they will automatically be returned to the team's practice squad after the game. Both are active for the contest.

Denver will be without running back Tyler Badie , offensive lineman Kage Casey, tight end Dallen Bentley, defensive lineman Jordan Jackson and defensive tackle Tyler Onyedim. Sam Ehlinger has been designated as the Broncos' emergency quarterback.

The Broncos did not have any player listed for Monday with an injury status, meaning that all of their inactive players are healthy scratches. Monday's official NFL transactions report showed that the Broncos released veteran wideout Lil'Jordan Humphrey before the game.

The Broncos have elevated long snapper Mitchell Fraboni and running back Adam Prentice for the matchup. Both will dress for the game.

articles.title: Landon Dickerson Says He 'Played Like S--t,' Updated Eagles OL Depth Chart with Guard Placed on IR
articles.summary: After hobbling through the Philadelphia Eagles' season opener against the Washington Commanders, Landon Dickerson is going on the injured reserve.
articles.body:
After hobbling through the Philadelphia Eagles' season opener against the Washington Commanders, Landon Dickerson is going on the injured reserve.

Per Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer, the left guard has been playing with a variety of injuries and will now miss at least the next four games.

Dickerson admitted Monday that he didn't play well and added that he suffered an injury in practice before the season.

"Honestly, I played like s--t yesterday. I was a complete liability. It was my fault. I should not be out there until I feel healthy," Dickerson said on WIP Radio (h/t John Clark of NBC Sports). "A few weeks ago, someone rolled up on me in practice. We got some imaging on it today. Really the best plan going forward is to put me on IR so I can have a good stretch at the back end of the season. I don't think anybody wants to see that again. That was ugly. That was BS. This is not related to last season."

A specific injury hasn't been reported, but it seems Dickerson was playing through a handful of ailments against the Commanders. That would explain his 25.9 pass-block grade from Pro Football Focus , which ranked 57th of 59 eligible guards. His run blocking was slightly better, but he still received a 47.5 grade from PFF.

Despite his struggles in Week 1, Nick Sirianni praised Dickerson for his effort in Week 1.

"His extreme power," Sirianni told reporters on Monday. "He's a big man who's able to move guys off the spot. If you go back and you look at. ... Okay, so he gives up some pressures. All right. But he also caved in the side on Saquon's long run on that third down and just did a really good job of pushing their defensive tackle and displacing him, which is a big job description for him. He's tough as heck. We've won a ton of games with Landon and there's a lot of good things that he can do."

Dickerson, a three-time Pro Bowler, dealt with a number of injuries during the 2025 campaign. He underwent knee surgery ahead of the season and later suffered back and ankle injuries. Still, he managed to appear in all but two games for the Eagles.

Amid the injury-filled year, there was some speculation that Dickerson would retire at just 27 years old, but he ultimately decided to return.

With Drew Kendall seemingly set to take over for Dickerson while he's on the injured reserve, it will mark the second career start for the 2025 fifth-round pick. Kendall appeared in eight games as a rookie, starting one.

The Eagles handled business against the Commanders in Week 1 and should have a relatively easy matchup against the Tennessee Titans this week. Things get tough after that, though, as they'll face the Chicago Bears, Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars in consecutive weeks.

articles.title: Inspiring story on friendship:“He means the world to me, he’s a guy that has really kind of made me who I am in my career”- How Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce built a brotherhood that goes far beyond football
articles.summary: NFL News: Some NFL partnerships are built on timing, talent and hours of practice. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have all of that, but their story goes furth.
articles.body: Some NFL partnerships are built on timing, talent and hours of practice. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have all of that, but their story goes further. What began when a young quarterback arrived in Kansas City has grown into a friendship that both players describe in deeply personal terms. Their connection has helped shape the Chiefs’ success, yet its greatest strength may have little to do with what happens on the field.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce found an instant connectionWhen Mahomes entered the NFL, Kelce was already an established presence in Kansas City. The quarterback was still learning what it took to lead an NFL team, while the tight end had already earned the trust of his teammates.The two quickly discovered that they approached football in a similar way. They wanted to compete, improve and win, but they also understood the importance of enjoying the journey.That shared mindset became the foundation of their relationship.Mahomes later explained that their connection was unusual because players do not always develop that kind of understanding immediately. For him, Kelce became someone he could trust when the pressure was at its highest.Their chemistry soon became one of the most difficult combinations for opposing defenses to contain. A Mahomes throw and a Kelce catch could change a game in seconds. But behind those spectacular moments was something less visible: countless practices, conversations and repetitions that helped the two understand each other almost instinctively.Mahomes has never treated that bond as simply a football partnership.“He means the world to me, man,” Mahomes, 29, told reporters after the Chiefs defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 19-17 on December 8, 2024. “Without getting emotional, he’s a guy that has really kind of made me who I am in my career.”That admission carried weight because Mahomes was speaking about someone who had been beside him through the most important stages of his professional life.Travis Kelce became more than a teammate to Patrick MahomesMahomes has repeatedly highlighted qualities in Kelce that fans cannot always see during a game.“A true leader on the football field,” Mahomes continued about Kelce. “Someone I can just go to at any moment and he’s going to make a big play happen. As he’s done throughout his career, he’s never dropped off as far as his work ethic and the way he leads. I think that’s super important.”That leadership became particularly meaningful as Mahomes grew into the face of the Chiefs.Kelce was not simply the player Mahomes looked for on third down. He was an experienced teammate who understood the demands of performing under enormous expectations. Their relationship gave Mahomes someone who could share the pressure rather than simply watch from the sidelines.In the same conversation, Mahomes called Kelce “the hardest working dude on the team.”That description says plenty about why their friendship has lasted. Fame can make relationships complicated, especially when two teammates become global stars. Yet Mahomes has continued to speak about Kelce in terms of trust, respect and gratitude.“He plays on the same wavelength that I do,” Mahomes added. “It’s hard to do that. It takes guys time. But from the first day, I’ve kind of been on that same page with Trav. Seeing him work every day — everybody sees the personality on the TV and stuff like that — but you don’t see that every day work ethic that he has. He’s the guy that gets mad when they take him out of practice routes.”The quote offers an important glimpse into their bond. The public sees Kelce’s personality, celebrations and confidence. Mahomes sees the teammate who keeps working when nobody is watching.Their NFL success strengthened the friendshipThe results of their partnership are remarkable.Mahomes and Kelce became central figures in a Chiefs era that delivered sustained success and multiple Super Bowl victories. Their connection turned into one of the most recognizable quarterback-tight end partnerships in modern NFL history.But success also brought difficult moments.Not every pass became a touchdown. Not every season ended with a championship. Their careers have included disappointing losses, criticism and stretches when the offense failed to produce at its usual level.During the 2024 season, Kelce openly admitted that his lack of touchdowns had become frustrating.“Where I take a lot of pride is once we get in that red zone, man,” Kelce said on his “New Heights” podcast. “I get a little hungrier. Right now, for whatever reason this year, I just can’t find my way in the end zone. I’m just not on the same page as Pat. It can get frustrating. It can get f—ing frustrating. That’s for damn sure.”Yet even when their numbers were not what they wanted, the relationship remained intact.That may be the real lesson in their friendship. Great partnerships are not tested only when everything goes right. They are tested when expectations are missed and confidence takes a hit.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce’s bond can outlast footballThe most meaningful part of the Mahomes-Kelce story may be what happens after the final whistle of their careers.Football gave them the opportunity to meet. It gave them a shared goal and countless unforgettable moments. But their friendship developed beyond the basic demands of the sport.Mahomes has spoken about how their families have also grown close, another sign that their relationship is no longer limited to the Chiefs locker room.That is why the word “brother” fits their story better than “teammate.”Kelce has helped Mahomes during the quarterback’s rise, while Mahomes has given Kelce a quarterback capable of matching his ambition and trusting him in the biggest moments. They have challenged one another, celebrated together and endured disappointment side by side.For Mahomes, the gratitude is personal.“He means the world to me, man,” he said.Those words explain why their friendship has become such a compelling part of the Chiefs story. Statistics will eventually fade. Records will eventually be broken. Players will eventually leave the game.The bond between Mahomes and Kelce, however, appears to have become something that football cannot easily measure.Their greatest achievement may not be a touchdown, a championship or a record. It may simply be that two teammates found a genuine friend in each other, then turned that friendship into a brotherhood that could last long after their NFL careers are over.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Robert Kraft, Gillette Stadium boot Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour over ‘Free Palestine’ rant
articles.summary: Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran's U.S. stadium tour after Robert Kraft's Gillette Stadium barred him over antisemitism allegations, grandstanding
articles.body: Macklemore is learning the hard way that concertgoers paying top dollar for stadium shows do not want a lecture on Middle Eastern geopolitics from the guy who wrote "Thrift Shop." Macklemore was kicked off Ed Sheeran’s U.S. stadium tour after multiple venues refused to host him following his pro-Palestinian speeches and performances at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The fallout escalated when New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft barred him from performing at Gillette Stadium, where Sheeran is scheduled to play Sept. 25 and 26. The rapper opened Sheeran’s shows at MetLife on Sept. 4 and 5. Macklemore wore a keffiyeh, showed footage of destruction in Gaza, performed "Hind’s Hall" and led the crowd in "Free Palestine" chants. The song includes lyrics accusing Israel of genocide. PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS Macklemore said the tour gave him a massive platform to promote his political message. He also claimed Sheeran told him Robert Kraft had rallied other stadium owners against keeping him on the tour. Kraft, whose Kraft Group owns Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, cited the rapper’s stage behavior and what he called a "broader history of anti-Semitic rhetoric and imagery." "Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," Kraft shared in a statement made to ESPN. "Based on Macklemore's recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran's shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of anti-Semitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th shows would not be permitted." Tour promoter Messina Touring Group confirmed Macklemore’s removal from all remaining U.S. dates after multiple venue operators refused to allow him on the lineup. Eight of the remaining 10 tour stops were scheduled for NFL stadiums. Macklemore’s controversial history includes a May 2014 performance in Seattle, where he took the stage wearing a bushy black beard, a dark wig and a large prosthetic nose. Civil rights groups, including the Anti-Defamation League, condemned the outfit as resembling historical anti-Jewish caricatures. Macklemore claimed at the time that the costume was a random coincidence. BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM That controversy resurfaced with the release of "Hind’s Hall," a song referencing student activists who occupied Columbia University’s Hamilton Hall. Critics argue that Macklemore routinely condemns Israel from the stage while ignoring the Oct. 7, 2023, terrorist attacks by Hamas that sparked the current war. Kraft, who founded the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism in 2019, also addressed what he viewed as Macklemore’s selective presentation of the conflict. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf," Kraft stated. "But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering." Kraft added that supporting innocent civilians while standing firmly against Hamas and antisemitism should not be mutually exclusive. "I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same: peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate," Kraft said. KACEY MUSGRAVES DIVIDES FANS WITH IMMIGRANT CHILDREN’S PLEA, FACES BOYCOTT CALLS TO ‘SHUT UP AND SING’ Macklemore responded in a social media post blaming venue operators and Kraft for his removal while acknowledging that Sheeran had been placed in a difficult position. He did not accept Kraft’s characterization of his comments as hate speech and insisted that losing his tour spot was a price he was willing to pay. articles.title: Malik Nabers Seemingly Shades Brian Daboll, Praises Giants' Harbaugh for Reaction in Injury Return
articles.summary: It seems like New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers is a bigger fan of his newest NFL head coach than his first one.
articles.body:
It seems like New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers is a bigger fan of his newest NFL head coach than his first one.

Nabers took to Instagram after helping lead his team to a 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday and posted a picture of himself celebrating with new head coach John Harbaugh and captioned it, "Never had this befo!! Dass love coach ❤️"

The wide receiver saying he never had that before it notable, as the Giants were coached by Brian Daboll when they selected him with the No. 6 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft.

Yet Daboll didn't last long, as New York fired him during the 2025 campaign and replaced him with interim coach Mike Kafka. But Nabers was limited to just four games last season because of injury, meaning he never played when Kafka was the interim coach.

Sunday marked his first game back since Sept. 28 of last year, and he wasted no time making an impact with six catches for 69 yards. Only Giants tight end Isaiah Likely had more catches or receiving yards in the game with eight receptions for 78 yards and two scores.

The Giants looked like a completely different team than the one that went 4-13 in 2025.

Jaxson Dart threw three touchdowns to zero interceptions, the rushing attack compiled 165 yards on the ground, and the defense picked off Dak Prescott while holding the Cowboys to just 3.8 yards per carry.

Harbaugh's first season at the helm is off to quite the start, and Nabers is already feeling the love.

articles.title: Broncos Eyed Drew Brees as Bo Nix Injury Replacement in New Rumors on QB Mulling Ending Retirement
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos were forced to play Jarrett Stidham in their AFC Championship Game loss to the New England Patriots last season after Bo Nix fractured his ankle the previous round, but they reportedly first considered one of the greatest signal-callers in NFL history.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos were forced to play Jarrett Stidham in their AFC Championship Game loss to the New England Patriots last season after Bo Nix fractured his ankle the previous round, but they reportedly first considered one of the greatest signal-callers in NFL history.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday that Broncos then-offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael reached out to Drew Brees to see whether the 47-year-old was interested in returning for the AFC Championship Game.

According to Schefter, Brees said he would work out first to see if he was ready but decided against the idea when he experienced discomfort in his wrist.

There was plenty of familiarity in place, as Lombardi and Carmichael were both assistant coaches for the New Orleans Saints when Brees played for the NFC South team. Brees also played for and won a Super Bowl with Broncos head coach Sean Payton in New Orleans.

Notably, Schefter reported Lombardi and Carmichael reached out to Brees without consulting Payton. The idea was to see whether the quarterback would even be interested in coming back before realistically discussing it with the head coach.

Alas, the Broncos could have used the Hall of Famer.

They managed just seven points in a 10-7 loss to the Patriots. Stidham was 17-of-31 for 133 yards, one touchdown and one interception and struggled to generate any consistent momentum against the New England defense.

Had the offense been even slightly better, the Broncos could have reached the Super Bowl.

Schefter's report comes after Brees hinted he considered coming back during a February appearance on the New Heights podcast (1:12:00 mark) when he said, "I will say I've had some conversations, and I've had some moments. … I would say this: my body feels great. My mind, sharp as ever. Shoulder, wrist? Not having it."

He also said at the time "something happened where I thought there might be a chance where I could play that week."

Brees wouldn't have been the only notable quarterback comeback last season, as Philip Rivers returned to guide the Indianapolis Colts down the stretch of the 2025 campaign.

That delayed Rivers' Hall of Fame eligibility until 2031, which stands in stark contrast to Brees. Brees was a member of the 2026 Hall of Fame class but may have been forced to wait another five years if he did return.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes answers troubling questions about his serious knee injury on first drive of the Chiefs season
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes scored on a zig-zagging 15-yard touchdown run on the Kansas City Chiefs' first offensive drive of the 2026 NFL season opener.
articles.body: If you were wondering whether Patrick Mahomes would be his old self following the serious knee injury he suffered exactly nine months ago to the day that the Kansas City Chiefs opened their 2026 season on Monday night, then rest easy. The quarterback scored on a 15-yard run to culminate his team's first offensive drive of the season against the Denver Broncos and, honestly, the zigzagging dash to the end zone that he finished with a dive said something: He's baaaack! "That was definitely the moment physically where that kind of said all my [rehabilitation] work paid off," Mahomes said. "Like, I didn't feel anything. And it's still a process, I still have to keep getting better and better and stay on top of it. "But this is obviously a great first week." CHIEFS FACE CRITICAL 2026 SEASON WITH PATRICK MAHOMES RETURNING FROM ACL TEAR The Chiefs, which sunk to a 6-11 record last season, seem to be back as well. They pummeled a talented Denver Broncos team by riding a stifling defense and running back Kenneth Walker rushing for 173 yards and a touchdown. But Mahomes was the story. Look, it remains to be seen how the season ultimately unfolds for the Chiefs and for what many consider to be the NFL's top quarterback. Mahomes was by no means dominant, completing only 55 percent of his passes and throwing 2 TD passes and 1 interception. But that was not the focus. The focus was gauging Mahomes and his return to health. Could he function? Could he still run? Could he still cause problems for the defense? That first drive, with the quarterback showing no fear of being hit, made a statement that put the rest of the league on notice. "It gave me that confidence back and let me be out there and be myself," Mahomes said. TRUMP PRESSES KANSAS CITY BBQ RESTAURANT OWNER ON WHETHER PATRICK MAHOMES WILL START WEEK 1 OF NFL SEASON Mahomes, who is turning 31 later this week, did not get hit in organized team activity sessions in the spring. He didn't get hit in training camp. He didn't get hit in the preseason, because he didn't play in any of the Chiefs' three games. He was hit during the game and so that psychological obstacle is now moot. "I just wanted to play," Mahomes said. "It was great to get Patrick back in the mix there and knock a little rust off," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. "He hadn't had a chance to play and see things coming at him quite that fast, so I was proud of him and how he handled it." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Mahomes is wearing a lightweight brace on his left knee. He has said it does not deter him from moving as he did before his surgery, but he does eventually expect to shed the gear — perhaps as early as late in this season. Mahomes tore both the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament in his left knee during the Chiefs’ Dec. 14, 2025, game against the Los Angeles Chargers. He underwent surgery in Dallas the next day, with doctors repairing the torn ACL and LCL, and began rehabilitation almost immediately. The exceedingly quick timetable for having the surgery was part of a plan, Mahomes has said. While many doctors urge their player patients to wait until their inflammation goes down before having surgery, Mahomes said his doctors urged him to get the surgery before the inflammation took root. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Mahomes then committed to an intensive recovery program that included roughly seven hours of rehabilitation per day. All that led to Monday night. "Once you put him in the game, he's going to play and you better be confident in him running," Reid said. "The only thing I asked was that [he] get down and, for the most part, he did that." Just not on that touchdown run. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Kenneth Walker Thrives in Chiefs Debut, Amazes NFL Fans and Fantasy Football Managers vs. Broncos
articles.summary: When the Kansas City Chiefs signed Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III this offseason, they knew the running back would be a big part of their offense.
articles.body:
When the Kansas City Chiefs signed Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III this offseason, they knew the running back would be a big part of their offense.

In the Chiefs' Week 1 matchup against the Denver Broncos, he essentially was their entire offense.

Walker rushed for 173 yards on 23 carries and added 18 yards through the air on three receptions. He tallied two total touchdowns in the 31-10 win over the reigning divisional champs.

Fans and fantasy managers were blown away by the former Seattle Seahawk in his first game with his new team.

Walker, a second-round pick in 2022, has had a strong start to his career, eclipsing 1,000 rushing yards twice, including last year when he rushed for 1,027 yards and five touchdowns.

But after the Chiefs' season opener, he appears on his way to a career season, especially if offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy continues to use him at the rate he did in Week 1.

It's not too surprising to see Walker get so many touches against Denver, considering the Broncos' tremendous pass rush and outstanding secondary anchored by Pat Surtain II. Patrick Mahomes was also in his first game back from a torn ACL and is still finding his rhythm.

That said, the Chiefs clearly like Walker, and he'll continue to be a huge part of the offense.

Kansas City has been looking for an elite running back, and Walker could be the missing piece that gets it back to the Super Bowl. And for fantasy managers with Walker on their roster, they could be in for a big year.

articles.title: At 36 and entering season 14, Travis Kelce finally explains why retirement still feels impossible
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is 36, has three Super Bowl rings, a booming podcast, and a life most athletes only dream about after hanging up their cleats. Yet here h.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is 36, has three Super Bowl rings, a booming podcast, and a life most athletes only dream about after hanging up their cleats. Yet here he is, preparing for his 14th NFL season with the Kansas City Chiefs. Before the season opener against the Denver Broncos, Kelce sat down with ESPN's Chris Berman alongside Patrick Mahomes on "Good Morning America" and said something that cut through all the noise: "I love this game so much that I'm not ready to go into that next phase yet."Why can't Travis Kelce walk away from football?The easy answer is legacy. The real answer is simpler than that.Kelce told Berman he still has "the desire to go out there and compete," and more importantly, he still believes he can. That belief matters more than any external timeline. At an age when most tight ends are already two years into retirement, Kelce is not chasing records or rings. He is chasing that feeling."I still think I can compete at a high level," he said.That is not bravado. For a player who has redefined what the tight end position looks like in modern football, it is a reasonable claim. The 2025 season was rough for Kansas City. No playoff run, questions everywhere. But Kelce came back, not because he had something to prove to critics, but because walking away from something you genuinely love is harder than it looks from the outside."I'm still kinda sitting here, like, 'I don't wanna let this thing go,'" he admitted.There is something quietly rare about that. Athletes at Kelce's level often talk about competitive fire in rehearsed, polished ways. This felt different. It felt like a man being honest about not being ready, and that honesty landed.What has changed for Kelce heading into the 2026 NFL Season?Plenty, actually.His life off the field looks nothing like it did five years ago. The "New Heights" podcast with his brother Jason has become one of the most-listened-to sports shows in the country. His presence in entertainment has grown steadily. By any conventional measure, Kelce has already built a second career that most athletes spend years scrambling to put together post-retirement.Andy Reid is still on the sideline. Mahomes is still under center. That continuity matters in ways that rarely get discussed. Kelce is not walking into an unfamiliar system or rebuilding trust with a new coaching staff. He is stepping back into something he knows deeply, and that familiarity likely makes the decision to return feel less like stubbornness and more like sense.How much longer will Travis Kelce keep playing in the NFL?Nobody knows, including Kelce.He wants "to keep playing until the wheels fall off." That is not a timeline, it is a philosophy. And for now, the wheels are intact.What makes this season worth watching is not whether Kelce puts up monster numbers. It is whether a player who has genuinely squeezed everything out of the game can find one more reason to love it. Based on everything he said before week one, he already has.Season 14 is not a farewell tour. Not yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Kenneth Walker is quietly becoming the most important player on the Chiefs' roster
articles.summary: NFL News: Kenneth Walker had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half of Kansas City's Week 1 matchup against the Denver Broncos. He set up a Mahomes touchdown.
articles.body: Kenneth Walker had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half of Kansas City's Week 1 matchup against the Denver Broncos. He set up a Mahomes touchdown on the opening drive. Then added two receptions. Then a 28-yard carry that was the longest play of the game. For a Chiefs team returning from a 6-11 collapse and a quarterback still finding his footing after ACL surgery, Walker did not just contribute. He carried the offense. And that was only the first half.Why is Kenneth Walker the Chiefs' most important player right now?Patrick Mahomes is the name on the marquee, but Walker is the reason this offense functions. That sounds like an overstatement. It isn't. When the Chiefs signed Walker to a three-year deal worth up to $45 million in March, the move was framed as a backfield upgrade. What it actually was, was a structural fix.Kansas City has not had a 1,000-yard rusher since Mahomes took over as the starting quarterback. That is a stunning gap for a team that won multiple Super Bowls. The passing game covered it up for years. Then Mahomes tore his ACL in Week 15 of 2025, the Chiefs went 6-11, and suddenly the absence of a credible ground game was impossible to ignore.Walker is also reviving something that had gone dormant in Andy Reid's offense for years: the screen game. During Reid's early tenure with Kansas City, Jamaal Charles gave him the personnel to run one of the most dangerous screen attacks in the NFL. That element has been absent since. Walker, who told Kay Adams he had been working directly with Mahomes to build passing game chemistry, averaged fewer than 40 catches per season in Seattle. That number is expected to jump considerably here.According to Jesse Newell of The Athletic, Reid opened up his screen-game playbook in training camp and Walker was the primary target, flashing strong receiving skills and even occasional one-handed catches.What makes Kenneth Walker different from every other Chief running back in recent memory?Walker forced 77 missed tackles across the 2025 regular season and playoffs, trailing only Bijan Robinson over that span, while earning a 91.4 PFF grade. He has improved his overall PFF grade every single season of his career. That kind of consistency is rare. So is his running style.At his July training camp press conference, Walker explained how patience and explosiveness coexist in his game. "I would just believe over the years running the ball since growing up, and just working with my pops, just seeing the defense is I believe that's how I really learned how to be patient or, you know, explosive. It just depends on what the play is, honestly," Walker said. "I feel like that helps the O-Line...whatever they need me to do, that's what I'm gonna do."The Chiefs have no real competition for passing-down work behind Walker. After waiving Emari Demercado, the remaining backs on the roster are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without the size to reliably block. The result is a roster built around giving Walker every snap they can justify.The Chiefs internally view Walker as a three-down back. That is not a label Kansas City has applied to a running back in a long time.How does Walker's role with the Chiefs compare to his time in Seattle?This is where context matters. Walker spent four years in Seattle largely underused, splitting touches with Zach Charbonnet and never fully earning a bell-cow role until Charbonnet's knee injury forced the Seahawks' hand late in the 2025 season. His usage in Seattle prior to that injury was likely a team preference rather than any reflection on Walker himself.In Super Bowl LX, Walker ran for 135 yards on 27 carries with two receiving touchdowns as Seattle defeated New England 29-13. He became the first running back to win Super Bowl MVP since Terrell Davis did it for Denver in Super Bowl XXXII.Kansas City did not sign a complementary piece. They signed a player whose ceiling had been artificially suppressed for years. The difference is real. In Seattle, Walker worked within a system that never fully committed to him. In Kansas City, the system is being designed around what he does.Week 1 against Denver was one data point. But the role, the contract, the scheme, and the 28-yard burst that stopped a stadium cold in the first half all point toward the same thing. Walker is not a piece of the Chiefs' rebuild. He is the foundation of it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chiefs Beat Broncos, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mahomes, Walker, Kelce, Nix, Waddle, More
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are back.
articles.body:
After missing the playoffs last season for the first time since the 2014 campaign, Kansas City bounced back in style during its 2026 opener with a commanding 31-10 victory over the rival Denver Broncos on Monday at Arrowhead Stadium.

Offseason addition Kenneth Walker III was brilliant, while Patrick Mahomes worked through some rust with multiple touchdown passes. The Chiefs defense also overwhelmed Bo Nix and kept the Denver offense in check for the majority of the contest.

The biggest storyline coming into this game was the return of the quarterbacks. It was Mahomes' first game back from the torn ACL and LCL that cut his 2025 campaign short, while Nix was back in the lineup after he missed the AFC Championship Game due to a fractured ankle.

Naturally, they were front and center right from the start for different reasons.

Nix threw an interception to Mansoor Delane on Denver's first possession, and the Chiefs took advantage on the ensuing drive when Mahomes broke free for a 15-yard rushing touchdown. His ability to dial up the speed in the open field seemed to answer any questions about whether he was physically ready, although he struggled with accuracy at times in the first half.

He struggled with accuracy, that is, until he found Rashee Rice for a touchdown pass right before intermission to answer Nix's touchdown pass to Evan Engram. The strike to Rice was a break from the Chiefs offense for the majority of the half, which was largely reliant on Walker.

But it was just a temporary break, as the home team continued to ride Walker to start the second half when he exploded to the outside and outran the entire Denver defense for a 60-yard touchdown to open up a two-score lead.

Walker's run was the biggest play of a second half largely defined by the Broncos' inability to get out of their own way.

When the visitors had an opportunity to climb right back in the game after Brandon Jones returned an interception of Mahomes to the Chiefs' 5-yard line, they had to settle for a field goal after a holding. When their defense held Kansas City to just a field goal after Travis Kelce's 59-yard reception moved him up in the history books, Nix lost a fumble.

That fumble recovery by Chris Jones set up yet another Walker touchdown as the new running back continued his dominance.

The Chiefs cruising against a team that was in last season's AFC Championship Game even with Mahomes playing at less than his best felt like a warning to the rest of the conference. With Walker now in the backfield and a strong defense on the other side, another deep playoff run would be anything but surprising.

And they will look to continue building on their early momentum with a Week 2 showdown with the Indianapolis Colts. As for Denver, it will attempt to bounce back against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Travis Kelce passes Jason Witten on all-time TE receiving yards list with wild 59-yard grab in win over Broncos
articles.summary: Travis Kelce entered Monday night's game just 44 yards shy of Jason Witten on the all-time receiving yards list.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce passed Jason Witten on Monday night, thanks largely to a massive catch he brought down during the Kansas City Chiefs ' season-opening win over the Denver Broncos .

Kelce caught a short pass from Patrick Mahomes midway through the third quarter of their 31-10 win at Arrowhead Stadium , and took off as fast as he could. After shedding one tackle, he had so much room to work with that he nearly made it all the way to the end zone. Finally, he was brought down inside Denver's 5-yard line.

The 36-year-old, who is listed at 6-foot-5, 250 pounds, nearly hit 17 mph at his peak during that run. In total, Kelce made it 59 yards on the catch. That eventually led to a field goal, which put the Chiefs up 24-10 at the time.

They added one more touchdown and rolled the rest of the way to secure the 21-point win .

The catch was Kelce's second of the night. It was more than enough to move him past Witten on the NFL's all-time receiving yards list for tight ends. Witten racked up 13,046 receiving yards during his career with the Dallas Cowboys . Kelce entered this season 44 yards shy of Witten's mark.

Kelce finished the game with 71 yards on three catches. That brought him to 13,073 in his career, which is good for second on the all-time list. Only Hall of Famer and former Chiefs star Tony Gonzalez is ahead of him. Gonzalez had 15,127 receiving yards in his career.

Kelce is the only active tight end even remotely close to Gonzalez's record. Free agent Zach Ertz has 8,592 receiving yards in his career, and San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle just surpassed the 8,000-yard mark.

Kelce still has a ways to go to catch Gonzalez. But record aside, his 14th NFL season got off to the perfect start.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III runs all over Denver as Chiefs beat up Broncos 31-10
articles.summary: Kansas City’s new running back put up 173 yards with two touchdowns; QB Patrick Mahomes threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another.
articles.body: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns in his Chiefs debut, stealing some of the spotlight from Patrick Mahomes and his surgically repaired left knee, and Kansas City exacted some revenge on the Denver Broncos for stealing its AFC West crown with a 31-10 victory Monday night. Mahomes didn’t appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, throwing for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as division champs. Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star also had three catches for 18 yards. The Broncos, meanwhile, were abysmal on offense in their first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays. Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and the Broncos finished with 176 yards of offense, all despite the offseason splash they made by trading a package of draft picks to Miami for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Waddle had one catch for 2 yards. Evan Engram led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards and their lone TD. The big question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason program and every practice of training camp, was how his surgically repaired left knee would hold up nine months to the day since he was hurt in a game against the Chargers. He erased any doubts when he capped the Chiefs’ opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run. It was Walker who did most of the running, though. The Super Bowl MVP for Seattle, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal in free agency, had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half alone, along with a couple of catches out of the backfield. The Broncos tied the game on Nix’s 19-yard touchdown pass to Engram, but Walker carried the load as the Chiefs pieced together a 10-play, 80-yard drive late in the half. It ended when Mahomes found Rashee Rice, fresh off a knee injury of his own, and he caromed off a couple of Broncos defenders and into the end zone to make it 14-7 at the break. Then it was Walker’s turn to bounce off a defender, turning a fourth-and-1 carry into a 60-yard TD run to start the third quarter. The teams traded field goals later in the quarter thanks to big plays by each side: Brandon Jones intercepted Mahomes deep in Chiefs territory, setting up Wil Lutz’s chip shot, and then Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 59 yards to set up Harrison Butker’s field goal. Nix’s fumble on the ensuing possession allowed the Chiefs to put the game away. Mahomes hit rookie running back Emmett Johnson on third down for a 26-yard gain, setting up first-and-goal at the Denver 2. And in the kind of creative — daresay, fun? — play that was reminiscent of the Chiefs’ banner years, Mahomes lined up in a three-point stance alongside backup QB Justin Fields, took the snap and shoveled the ball to Walker, who scooted untouched for the score.

articles.title: Sean Payton on Broncos' play-calling in Davis Webb's debut: 'Lotta throws, not enough runs'
articles.summary: The Broncos' offensive performance in offensive coordinator Davis Webb's play-calling debut was not what you would call a rousing success.
articles.body:
The Broncos ' offensive performance in coordinator Davis Webb 's play-calling debut was not what you would call a rousing success. The Chiefs dominated the Broncos and held Bo Nix and the offense in check in Kansas City 's 31-10 victory.

Nix was intercepted and lost a fumble, was sacked three times by the Chiefs and was ineffective as a runner. As a team, the Broncos totaled 176 yards and scored only three points after their first-quarter touchdown.

Broncos head coach Sean Payton relinquished play-calling — his baby for 18 years as a head coach — to the 31-year-old Webb this offseason after Webb had received some head-coaching attention from around the league. With it came a promotion and Payton bequeathing Webb the ceremonial Denny's menu.

Payton never mentioned Webb postgame by name but did point out that the Broncos' issues start with the coaching staff, himself included.

"Obviously, not a good evening. Didn't do a lot well at all in the game," Payton said. "We'll get a chance to look at the tape tomorrow, but I felt like all the key factors … they rushed the ball well, we didn't. That starts with me. That starts with our coaching staff. I thought they won in really every phase."

This is still nominally Payton's offense. It's still catered to Nix's strengths and weaknesses, at least in theory. The Nix-Webb relationship was a big selling point for the change. But the first time with Webb in Nix's ear didn't go well.

Payton said there were "a number of places we have to look" after Webb's first time with the call sheet.

"Our third-down numbers weren't good. Our rushing numbers weren't good. Pick your spot," Payton said.

Sean Payton's halftime interview was an eyebrow raiser

Payton appeared to send a veiled message to his new coordinator with his halftime interview with ESPN's Laura Rutledge when she asked Payton what more he wanted to see out of Bo Nix .

"I think the first thing we have to do is rush the ball a little more efficiently. That'll take some pressure off [Nix]," Payton said. "Right now, we've been in a bit of a pass mode. I think it's the opposite for Kansas City. They've been able to run the ball. I think that needs to switch a little in the second half."

When asked how not calling plays went in the first half, Payton said: "Ask me in another half here."

For what it's worth, the Broncos handed off 12 times all game — six in each half. Payton mentioned more than once that Denver 's rushing disparity held the offense back, even while noting that some RPO runs turned into pass plays.

"Lotta throws, not enough runs," Payton said.

The Broncos' 177 yards were fewer even than their total (181) in the AFC championship game, with Jarrett Stidham replacing an injured Nix in a game that was played in a blizzard. Denver's nine first downs matched their 2025 season low, which they hit in a dud of a win over the Raiders — a reminder that Payton has off days, too.

Payton was asked whether it was tougher to watch the offensive struggles given that he didn't have full control over what was being called.

"Look, it was, just as a head coach always, whether you're calling plays or not, regardless of who's calling the plays, when you have a game like that and you're the head coach, it's frustrating. It's disappointing. And I don't know if the feeling's any different if you're calling them or not," Payton said.

To the Chiefs' credit, the defense, led by coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, was spectacular. They tackled well — unlike the Broncos — and kept everything short. The Broncos' long gain was Evan Engram 's 19-yard TD strike, which was a rare offensive highlight on the night.

Denver's script went dry after that. The Broncos gained only 109 yards on the remaining 37 plays in the game. Penalties wiped out some positive plays and put Denver in longer-yardage situations. Webb's struggles mirrored the tepid results of two other young play-calling former backup QBs, Sean Mannion and David Blough , who faced off in Eagles-Commanders in Week 1.

Monday night was a brutal first test for Webb, but not a bye-week referendum. Unless Payton's play-calling itch gets the best of him, it's still Webb's job. There will be ample room for improvement in their next outing in Week 2 against a Jaguars team riding high after their statement victory over the Browns in Week 1.

articles.title: What did Peyton Manning say after Bo Nix’s costly interception? Denver Broncos suffer heartbreaking 31-10 loss to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs
articles.summary: NFL News: Bo Nix’s return to the Denver Broncos lineup could hardly have started worse. On Monday, Nix threw an interception on Denver’s first passing attempt a.
articles.body: Bo Nix’s return to the Denver Broncos lineup could hardly have started worse. On Monday, Nix threw an interception on Denver’s first passing attempt against the Kansas City Chiefs, leaving Peyton Manning visibly stunned during the ManningCast.The Hall of Fame quarterback watched Nix’s comeback from the ManningCast booth with his brother Eli Manning. Nix had not played a regular-season game since fracturing his ankle in Denver’s AFC Divisional Round win over Buffalo last season, and his first series at Arrowhead Stadium quickly gave Manning something to react to. Peyton Manning breaks down the interception that gave Chiefs an early openingThe problem started before Nix even got a chance to settle into the game. He took a sack on Denver’s opening play, ran on the second play and then dropped back on third down looking for Courtland Sutton.Chiefs rookie Mansoor Delane jumped the route and intercepted Nix, giving Kansas City possession at the Denver 46-yard line. Manning immediately reacted during the ManningCast alternate broadcast on ESPN2.“Oh, no, no, no, no,” Manning said during the Sept. 14 ManningCast while reacting to the interception.The Mannings then went through the coverage. Peyton initially read the play as a two-man look, while Eli pointed out that Kansas City actually had a single-high safety. Eli felt Delane guessed on the route and nearly stumbled into the interception.Peyton then explained why he viewed the play as a fortunate break for the rookie cornerback.“He’s lucky he ran the in route, because the trail technique without a safety help over the top, if you go deep, it’s going to be wide open,” Manning said during the ManningCast. “He really lucks out on that play.”That gave the Chiefs a chance to turn Nix’s mistake into points, and they did exactly that. Kenneth Walker III carried the ball seven times for 32 yards on the drive before Patrick Mahomes finished it with a 15-yard touchdown run. Bo Nix quickly answered Peyton Manning’s concernNix did not let the interception define his return. Denver’s next possession looked completely different, with the quarterback completing all five of his passes for 55 yards and ending the drive with a 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end Evan Engram. The score tied the game at 7-7.Manning acknowledged the response while continuing to point out how fortunate Delane had been on the earlier play. “He should have guessed right,” Manning said during the ManningCast. “Pretty good start to his career, Eli.”Nix’s quick response offered Denver an early lift, but the Broncos could not keep pace with Kansas City. The Chiefs eventually pulled away for a 31-10 victory at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14.The result also flipped the script from 2025. Denver had swept Kansas City in both meetings last season and won the AFC West for the first time in a decade. This time, Mahomes and the Chiefs opened the new season with a convincing win while Nix’s comeback began with one interception that had Peyton Manning shaking his head.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La NFL recupera a su gran estrella nueves meses después: el dulce regreso de Patrick Mahomes
articles.standfirst: Nueve meses y 274 días después de la operación rodilla Mahomes volvió como titula ante los Denver Broncos.
articles.summary: Nueve meses y 274 días después de la operación rodilla Mahomes volvió como titula ante los Denver Broncos.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes regresó tras nueve meses de baja por su lesión de cruzado y lo hizo de la forma más dulce y con un nuevo estelar socio, un Kenneth Walker MVP del último Super Bowl con Seattle, que destrozó a los Denver Broncos y entregó a los Kansas City Chiefs un triunfo por 31-10. Walker recorrió 173 yardas con 23 carreras y anotó un espectacular 'touchdown' tras un empuje de 60 yardas en su primer partido oficial con los Chiefs, después de su extraordinaria temporada acabada con el título con los Seattle Seahawks. Hizo más fácil la vida a Patrick Mahomes, que comenzó su partido con una carrera de quince yardas para anotar el 'TD' inaugural. Lanzó para 184 yardas (15 de 27 en pases), con dos pases de anotación, por una interceptación. En los Broncos, el mariscal de campo Bo Nix se quedó en 131 yardas, con un pase de 'touchdown' y una interceptación. Si Walker sumó 173 yards por tierra, los Broncos no pasaron de las 61 en total. Con su mujer, la estrella del pop Taylor Swift, en el palco, Travis Kelce se convirtió en el segundo jugador con más yardas recibidas en la NFL, al superar las 13.046 de Jason Witten. Solo tiene por delante a Tony González, con 15.127. Para el técnico de los Chiefs, Andy Reid, fue la decimoctava victoria de su carrera en el partido inaugural de sus equipos, con la que igualó el récord de Bill Belichick. Mahomes sufrió el 14 de diciembre de 2025 la rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior y lateral de la rodilla izquierda, en los instantes finales de la derrota ante Los Angeles Chargers. Aquella lesión cerró su campaña y dejó a Kansas City con una marca de 6-8, fuera de la lucha por los 'playoffs'. Nueve meses y 274 días después de la operación, Mahomes volvió como titular este lunes ante los Denver Broncos. El mariscal de campo utilizó una rodillera protectora en la articulación izquierda. Denver también llegó condicionado por el problema físico de Bo Nix, quien sufrió una fractura de tobillo en la ronda divisional de los 'playoffs' de la pasada temporada, ante Buffalo. La lesión se produjo en una carrera en tiempo extra, requirió cirugía y le impidió disputar el resto de la postemporada con los Broncos. La primera semana de la NFL dejó una exhibición ofensiva de los Chicago Bears, que vencieron 59-37 a los Carolina Panthers con 124 yardas y tres anotaciones por tierra de D'Andre Swift. Caleb Williams contribuyó con dos 'touchdowns' por tierra y otros dos mediante pases, en la tercera mayor anotación histórica de la franquicia. También se destacó Josh Allen, decisivo en el triunfo 36-31 de los Buffalo Bills frente a los Houston Texans con un envío de 34 yardas a Joshua Palmer en el último minuto. Philadelphia superó 24-22 a Washington, Minnesota arrolló 39-22 a Green Bay y Seattle abrió con un 13-10 contra New England.
