articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 2: What do we make of the Rams without Myles Garrett?
articles.summary: The Rams remain in the top 5 but for how long? Meanwhile the Niners and Giants made the biggest jumps in the league. Headed in the opposite direction: the Co...
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Los Angeles Rams losing a weird game in Australia, for which they gambled that an aggressive travel plan wouldn't affect them but were obviously wrong, isn't that bad. They played terribly but it's fine to excuse it to having to play across the world.

But then, after not posting a single stat in a quiet Rams debut, Myles Garrett said his knee wasn't feeling well. A few days later, it was reported that Garrett was having knee surgery. On Monday, Rams head coach Sean McVay said there's no timetable for Garrett's return . He'll be out at least four weeks on injured reserve.

The Rams came into the season as the clear Super Bowl favorite , and that's already in question. It's not just losing Garrett, the best defensive player in the NFL. Matthew Stafford is 38 and he looked awful in the opener. When Rich Gannon won his first NFL MVP at age 37, like Stafford did last season, he threw only nine touchdowns the rest of his career. The age cliff finds everyone. Davante Adams, at 33, was a non-factor in the opener against the 49ers. The defense around Garrett didn't play well. Maybe it was all Australia. Maybe not.

Going forward without Garrett for however long is scary for this defense. The Rams had to trade Jared Verse to Cleveland in the Garrett deal, so they now have a big hole at defensive end. Aaron Donald being a force after returning from two years off is a lot more questionable without Garrett around to command double teams. The 49ers gained 379 yards and had no problems in the air or on the ground. Again, maybe that's just fatigue from a long trip, but we don't know yet. We also don't know if the long trip will impact the Rams for a few weeks to come. The Rams face the Giants on Monday night in Week 2, and that matchup doesn't look so easy after the Giants played well in their opening-game win against the Cowboys.

It's typically not a good idea to overreact to Week 1. The Raiders won at New England in last season's opener. Las Vegas went 3-14 and the Patriots went 14-3. Weird things happen in the beginning. However, there should be concern about the Rams. Not enough to send them way down the rankings, but enough that their standing as the clear Super Bowl favorite, or even the favorite in the NFC West, is in question. It's a top-heavy team and there are significant worries about their stars just one week into the season. We might not get a clear picture of who the Rams are until Garrett returns and shows he's back to his normal self. Whenever that will be.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 1 of the NFL season:

Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said success wouldn't be defined by wins or losses but development, and while he got a hard time for saying it, it's true for the 2026 Dolphins. In that way, it was good to see rookies like linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (a game-high 14 tackles and he played all 68 defensive snaps) and receiver Caleb Douglas (five catches, 94 yards) play well. This team still has a significantly insufficient roster, hence why it is in this spot even though it didn't embarrass itself like the …

An argument can be made that the Titans deserve to be No. 32. No team looked worse in Week 1. Against a Jets team that was 3-14 last season, the Titans had seven first downs and three points before their final possession, when they trailed by 20 points. Tennessee forced one punt and zero turnovers in the first three quarters. If you get dominated by the Jets at home, it could be a very long season. It probably explains the booing that fans gave the Titans. "When you lose, you're a loser," head coach Robert Saleh bluntly said afterward , acknowledging the discontent. Could more be on the immediate horizon? Up next for the Titans is a home game against the Eagles.

The Browns' defense is supposed to keep them in games, even with Jared Verse replacing Myles Garrett. That wasn't the case in the opener as the Browns looked like they really missed Jim Schwartz as defensive coordinator. Trevor Lawrence had four touchdowns and Jacksonville had 31 points with 12:08 left in the third quarter. If Cleveland's defense is bad, there's no hope at a respectable season.

It's hard to get too excited about the start of the season when Cooper Rush is QB1. Head coach Kevin Stefanski gave no update Monday on who'll be the starter for Week 2 vs. the Panthers. Michael Penix Jr. might return soon, but will that fix much? Atlanta's defense played well in the Falcons' loss at Pittsburgh, but that probably has more to do with the Steelers' offense that was held to 3-of-13 on third downs and 0-for-2 on fourth. Despite the quagmire everywhere around him, Bijan Robinson still managed 83 rushing yards and 90 receiving yards. So there, Falcons fans have one reason to be excited.

It shouldn't be a surprise that the Cardinals looked good on offense. Their quarterback situation isn't ideal but they have good skill position players. The surprise of their season-opening upset win was Arizona's defense. The Chargers got just 268 yards, they sacked Justin Herbert three times and had an interception and fumble recovery. Andrew Wingard, who had the interception of Herbert, had something he partially got off his chest postgame. "Everyone has been trashing this defense, trashing coach [Nick] Rallis," Wingard said of his defensive coordinator . "It's like … I'm going to be polite and not say what I want to say, but — it's not gratifying because it'd only be gratifying if you cared about it, but I'm just happy for all these guys." Arizona was eighth in EPA ( expected points added ) allowed per play through Sunday's Week 1 games. The Cardinals were projected to have one of the NFL's worst defenses this season, but that wasn't the case in the opener. A matchup against the Seahawks now looks more interesting.

We'll likely look back at the Jets' Week 1 win and realize the Titans really are that bad. However, allowing 195 yards to any NFL team is impressive. The Jets gained 367 yards and generally looked sharp in all ways on offense. Head coach Aaron Glenn needs to show improvement this season and he's off to a great start, even if it was against Tennessee.

The focus was on the Bears' offense , but the Panthers' defense was part of that story. Carolina had never allowed more than 52 points in a game before allowing 59 on Sunday. The Panthers spent big on the defense in the offseason and the results for Week 1 were awful. They wasted a fantastic performance by Bryce Young, who had 361 yards and three touchdowns passing and rushed for another score. Defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero might be on the hot seat early this season. "Like I said, it's embarrassing, but ultimately, I'm taking a really positive outlook from this because we can only get better from here," Panthers outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips said, via the team's site .

The Raiders can thank the schedule makers. Getting Miami at home to start the season was great for a team that had so many changes, including a new head coach in Klint Kubiak. They still had to execute no matter the opponent and the Raiders did just that, winning 27-13. It was without tight end Brock Bowers, who will hopefully be back soon from a meniscus trim in his knee. It was a good start, though the Raiders had a good start last season with a win at New England. This time they have to build on it.

Daniel Jones returning for Week 1, a little more than nine months after tearing his Achilles, always felt aggressive. And Jones didn't play well in Week 1. He was 28th among 30 qualified quarterbacks in adjusted EPA per play through Sunday's Week 1 games. Pair that with a defense that allowed 506 yards to the Ravens, and there should be plenty of concern in Indianapolis after just one game.

The Saints have a rightful complaint that a defensive touchdown was taken off the board due to a convoluted explanation of why Jared Goff's pass that went backward was actually incomplete. With that play, the Saints probably win a game that they eventually lost in overtime. Still, being a 2-point conversion away from beating a talented Lions team on the road is a positive sign for the season.

Everything was labored with Jayden Daniels and the Commanders' offense . The line didn't protect well but Daniels often held the ball too long, perhaps because his receivers weren't getting open. He averaged 3.41 seconds per throw, the slowest among all QBs through Sunday's games, per Next Gen Stats. ( H/T to reporter Tashan Reed for pointing that out .) The Eagles have a good defense and that led to some of the issues. But the opener wasn't a good omen, especially for new coordinator David Blough. At least he has Daniels in his corner. The QB defended the shovel pass play that the Eagles stuffed on a 2-point conversion attempt, preventing a tie in the final minute of regulation. "It was the right call," Daniels told reporters postgame . "Anything Blough calls, man. I'm with him. Regardless, however everybody else might want to view it, man, I'm with Blough 100%."

The Buccaneers played well enough to win at the Bengals but they turned it over four times, one of which was returned for a touchdown and another that came at the Bengals' 4-yard line. You can't ignore that because it's a continuation of the sloppiness that cost the Bucs a division title last season. The good news for the Bucs is the division is still just as bad. Every NFC South team is 0-1.

The Steelers got a win but it wasn't pretty. Facing a Falcons team down to its third quarterback, the Steelers led by just three points in the fourth quarter before T.J. Watt had an interception return for a touchdown. Particularly troubling was the offense, which had the worst success rate in the NFL for Week 1. The run game really struggled, with 2.8 yards per carry. And that's against a Falcons defense that wasn't projected to be very good.

There's nothing good to say about the Chargers' Week 1 loss. It was so dispiriting that head coach Jim Harbaugh lamented sitting his starters for most of the preseason . The offense, with new coordinator Mike McDaniel, had two plays longer than 15 yards against an Arizona defense that isn't expected to be good. ( Don't tell Andrew Wingard I said that .) The defense, without last year's star coordinator Jesse Minter, allowed points or a missed field goal on seven of 10 possessions before a kneel-down at the end. The Chargers' early-season schedule is brutal , and the Cardinals game was supposed to be a rare easy win.

Nobody in Wisconsin wants to hear about how many yards Green Bay had or that the Packers outplayed the Vikings for most of the game. They want to know why the Packers, who lost five straight games last season, including multiple blown second-half leads, keep failing late in games. The Packers were outscored 22-0 in the fourth quarter. There has to be better answers for why the Packers are collapsing late. "It'll be a topic of conversation for all you guys until we do it," Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said . "That's the bottom line."

The Vikings won and that's a great way to start the season, but it's not like they played well. They were outgained 419-239. The Packers had 6.3 yards per play to just 3.9 for the Vikings. Minnesota won a game in which it lost Kyler Murray in the first quarter to a concussion, so squeezing out a victory is still a very good result but improvement needs to be made, and a lot of that will depend on Murray's status.

No team had a better EPA on offense than the Giants in Week 1 — which means no team had a worse EPA on defense than the Cowboys. Maybe team owner Jerry Jones was right to be "nervous" before kickoff Sunday night. Maybe everyone was too quick to assume that the Dallas' exhaustive defensive issues from a season ago were fixed. Despite new personnel and a new coordinator, the same communication issues that led to blown coverages showed up again in the loss to New York . Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones took a measured view of the wreckage, telling 105.3 The Fan (via The Athletic's Jon Machota ): "Felt really good and still do about our football team. We just probably had a little unrealistic expectations in terms of what we could do, especially on the defensive side of the ball with all the new faces and a brand new coordinator." Indeed, nobody should completely overreact to Week 1. But after a horrendous performance in the season opener, the Cowboys' defense now has to show evidence, starting Week 2 vs. the Commanders, it's any better than it was last season.

A lot will be made of coordinator Davis Webb taking over play-calling from Sean Payton and the Broncos' offense looking terrible in his first game doing it. That's not all that was wrong with Denver. The defense was rock solid last season but was miserable Monday night against the Chiefs. There were numerous missed tackles as the Chiefs rushed for more than 200 yards. The Broncos were very unlikely to replicate a 14-win season, but there was good reason to believe they were still capable of winning the AFC West again. They'll have to play far better on both sides of the ball if they want to keep the division race competitive this season.

No team had a better offensive EPA per play through Sunday's Week 1 games than the Giants. Not even the Bears, who scored 59 points. What stood out was the impact new tight end Isaiah Likely had. He led the Giants with eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns. If the Giants' offense stays mostly healthy, perhaps this can be a surprise playoff team.

The defense should be fine when it's not facing Josh Allen. If that's the case, the positive about the loss to the Bills is that the offense looked good. Houston ranked ninth in offensive success rate through Sunday's games behind an improved rushing attack with David Montgomery and quarterback C.J. Stroud playing better. Stroud had 274 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. If that carries over, Houston is going to be good this season.

The Bengals' defense looked better. The Bucs' offense scored just 20 points and had fewer than 300 yards. Turnovers aren't guaranteed to carry over week to week but the Bengals forced four, including one that was returned for a touchdown. Cincinnati isn't going to be great on defense, but there have been some good teams to live off having a great offense and a defense that takes chances and makes a few game-changing plays. Maybe the Bengals can be that type of defense. That would be enough.

The overreaction directed at Drake Maye proves that the hate of the Patriots hasn't died just because Bill Belichick and Tom Brady are long gone. Maye didn't play well in the opener and didn't have a good postseason either. He played elite defenses in almost every game though. Maye is going to be good. He's just not able to overcome a middling supporting cast — A.J. Brown was out for the second half and TreVeyon Henderson was inactive in the opener — against great defenses as a third-year player. He's not nearly as bad as you'll read on social media.

The Bears are going to be fun to watch . The offense was fantastic against a Panthers defense that isn't great but not that bad (22nd in defensive DVOA last season). They put up 59 points, a franchise record for a season opener, and 552 yards. That's great. They also allowed 37 points and 478 yards against a Panthers offense that was 25th in DVOA last season. Every game might be a pinball machine. And the Bears' offense might be so good it doesn't matter how much the defense allows. It's why they're not higher in the top 10.

The Lions almost blew a 21-0 lead. They held on when they forced an incompletion on a 2-point conversion in overtime. Detroit's defense had played very well in building that lead, then let the Saints back in the game. Lions head coach Dan Campbell blamed the offense's inefficiency for the lead slipping away. "I'm like, man, we've got to be more efficient on offense," Campbell said . "We kind of spit and sputtered there and then they … had some tempo going."

The Lions face a very tough Week 2 game against the Bills, who will host their first regular-season game in their new stadium Thursday night.

The first look at new coordinator Sean Mannion's scheme wasn't great. Only the Steelers' offense had a lower success rate than the Eagles through Sunday's games. Jalen Hurts made some big plays, many of which were him creating something when nothing was open, and that saved the win. There's a long way to go for the offense.

Kenneth Walker III was excellent and will transform the Chiefs' offense. He had 173 yards rushing. Patrick Mahomes will be better as he get further removed from a torn ACL. He had just 184 yards passing and was off on many throws, but that didn't take away from a successful return. But one of the best stories of the opener was left tackle Kahlil Benson. He is an undrafted rookie out of Indiana who got no guaranteed money to sign with the Chiefs and did not play left tackle in college. He was forced into the lineup due to a Josh Simmons injury and there was rightful concern over him protecting Mahomes' blindside. But Benson, the first undrafted rookie to start Week 1 on the offensive line since Terence Steele with the Cowboys in 2020, played well and the Broncos rarely got any pressure on Mahomes. Offensive linemen don't get too much attention, but Benson deserves a lot of credit for stepping up when he had to.

The Jaguars were fantastic last season. There was nothing fluky about their season. Then they looked dominant in Week 1. They led 31-0 early in the third quarter and if they wanted to run it up, the final score could have been really ugly for Cleveland. Jacksonville was one of two teams in the NFL in the top six of EPA per play and EPA allowed per play through Sunday's Week 1 games (Baltimore was the other). The Jaguars deserve respect.

Few teams looked better than the 49ers in Week 1. It remains to be seen how the 49ers react to coming back from Australia, but their next two games are at home against the Dolphins and Cardinals. That helps. It's hard to buy that the 49ers can stay healthy — exciting rookie De'Zhaun Stribling suffered an ankle injury that will keep him out at least a month — but if they can then San Francisco showed it can be as good as anyone.

We can't throw out everything we know because of one game. Maybe the Rams will be a huge disappointment this season, but it's too early to proclaim that. The Rams were the second-best team in the NFL last season and had a good offseason even before the Myles Garrett trade. Throughout the rankings, you'll see some teams that didn't move very much due to a great or bad Week 1. It's a one-game sample size for now.

Had it not been for the Bears, we'd be talking more about how good the Ravens' offense looked. They gained 502 yards, and that was with a conservative second-half approach after losing receivers Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to injuries. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle was Ben Johnson's coordinator last season and the Ravens seem to have made a great hire with him. Keeping Lamar Jackson healthy is important, and the early receiver injuries are concerning, but the Ravens looked like a Super Bowl contender in Week 1.

More disrespect for the Seahawks to not be No. 1. Your anger is understandable, Seattle fans. But the Sam Darnold injury sets the Seahawks back a bit until he returns. But there's no question about Seattle's defense, which was excellent against the Patriots and carried the team to a win. Maybe that's enough to carry the team as long as Drew Lock is at quarterback.

Had Bills-Texans happened in prime time, as it should have, we'd be even more excited about what Josh Allen did against a very good Houston defense. The 36 points the Bills put up was the most against Houston since 2023, which was DeMeco Ryans' first season as head coach. Allen threw for 334 yards and two touchdowns and rushed for 23 yards and two touchdowns. That win was a statement. The fact that it happened in the 1 p.m. Eastern window just means the Bills won't get as much hype as they should. That might change Thursday night when they face the Lions.

articles.title: Sean Payton Reacts to Broncos' 'Frustrating' Loss to Chiefs, Giving Up Play-Calling to Davis Webb
articles.summary: Davis Webb's first game as the Denver Broncos' play-calling was one to forget.
articles.body:
Davis Webb's first game as the Denver Broncos' play-calling was one to forget.

Broncos head coach Sean Payton made headlines this offseason when he revealed he was giving up play-calling duties to the team's new offensive coordinator, but Denver managed just 10 points in Monday's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.

"Just as a head coach always, whether you're calling the plays or you're not. Regardless of who's calling the plays. When you have a game like that, and you're the head coach, you know it's frustrating," Payton told reporters after the season-opening loss (1:30 mark).

Kenneth Walker III goes off in Chiefs debut

"It's disappointing. And I don't know that the feeling is any different, whether you're calling them or not. Honestly."

Denver scored its touchdown in the opening quarter but didn't find the end zone the rest of the way as it struggled in the aerial attack and on the ground.

Quarterback Bo Nix went 17-of-28 for 131 yards, one touchdown and one interception while also losing a fumble. The rushing attack managed just 61 yards on the ground, and no pass-catcher eclipsed tight end Evan Engram's 43 yards.

Payton also discussed the play-calling during a halftime interview with ESPN:

The Chiefs enjoyed a commanding 392-176 advantage in total yards with Kenneth Walker III (173 rushing yards and 18 receiving yards) tallying more offensive production than the entire Denver unit.

While this was Webb's first game as the play-caller in the offensive coordinator role, he was a quarterbacks coach for the Broncos the past three seasons. He is familiar with Nix and the offense and will surely be given another opportunity to turn things around after Monday's loss.

But the offense will have to be much better than it was in the opener if the Broncos are once again going to win the AFC West.

articles.title: 3 takeaways from the Chiefs’ season-opening beatdown of the Broncos
articles.summary: Here are some thoughts from Kansas City’s dominant Week 1 win.
articles.body:
What a night it was for the Kansas City Chiefs .

Facing the reigning AFC West champions, a team that took the division's throne from the Chiefs after Kansas City's nine-year run sitting upon it, the dynastic Chiefs made a statement:

With that theme from Monday night, here are three fresh takes from Kansas City's reminder to the NFL:

You may have heard local media and certain bloggers talk about the Chiefs' offensive identity shift to an under-center, run-centric approach this offseason.

I can't speak for everybody, but even the most optimistic version of myself didn't see this coming.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes was under center plenty on Monday night, and that's the way running back Kenneth Walker prefers it, as he told Kay Adams back in May . Walker did something Chiefs fans haven't seen from a member of their favorite team's backfield since 2016!

The Chiefs' offense not only adjusted to fit its personnel best, but the coaching staff also stayed committed to the game plan through a couple of stalled drives in the first half. Kansas City punted three consecutive possessions after the opening-drive touchdown, but the offense continued to ride Walker and a downhill ground attack.

It's a reminder that head coach Andy Reid (and general manager Brett Veach) had a vision for this team and didn't waver from it since the start of the 2026 offseason. The makeover looks perfectly executed through one week.

2. This defense is very ahead of schedule

Like the 2022 Chiefs, this year's defense features rookies who will develop on the fly while playing prominent roles.

However, this year's unit may be ahead of schedule. Like, way ahead of schedule.

Cornerback Mansoor Delane showed off elite coverage skills from the jump. On the opening drive, Delane manned up wide receiver Courtland Sutton , sticking to his hip pocket and covering up the route so well that when he turned to defend the pass, he barely needed to react, and he had an interception.

Shortly after, Delane left the game with a shoulder injury, but one play is all it took for Delane to show why he could be one of the next elite cornerbacks in the NFL.

Up front, defensive end R Mason Thomas ignited a pass rush that tormented a Broncos offense that surrendered the fewest sacks in the NFL last season. Quarterback Bo Nix was sacked four times and fumbled three times. Defensive tackle Peter Woods flashed as a pass rusher too, batting down a pass at one point.

The 2022 Chiefs' defense allowed 21 points to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1 and 24 points (and 401 total yards) to the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. There were clear growing pains early in that season; this year, it's harder to tell where these rookies need to improve.

It took a while for the Chiefs' offense to get over 15 passing yards. It was almost comical how much of the offense's output was on Walker's shoulders for much of the game. In the first half, Mahomes had just two completions over 12 pass attempts; neither catch resulted in a first down.

In the second half, Mahomes was much more efficient. He completed 13 of 15 passes; eight of those catches resulted in a first down or a touchdown.

The commitment to the run game certainly helped the offense find a better dropback rhythm as the game went on. The biggest blemish in the second half seemed to be a miscommunication between Mahomes and wide receiver Xavier Worthy , one of the game's most frustrating storylines. The third-year wideout needs to get on the same page with Mahomes one way or another.

That said, Denver's pass defense is truly elite. Mahomes will find softer coverages to exploit, and continuing to run the ball will only help.

articles.title: Travis Kelce makes NFL history in 2026 season opener for Chiefs with wife Taylor Swift in attendance
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs TE Travis Kelce made history in the 2026 NFL season opener by advancing to No. 2 on the all-time receiving yards list for TEs.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs TE Travis Kelce made history in the 2026 NFL season opener by advancing to No. 2 on the all-time receiving yards list for TEs.

Kelce and the Chiefs got their season off to a winning start against the Denver Broncos with a dominant 31-10 win in Patrick Mahomes ' first game back in nine months.

While Mahomes' performance had plenty of valid criticisms around it, the 36-year-old Kelce showed the world, and his wife Taylor Swift, that his decision to play for another season was the right one.

Travis Kelce's 59-yard run in Chiefs game makes NFL history

Kelce got loose in the third quarter, catching a short pass from Mahomes and finding an open field for him to run up, getting brought down after 59 yards. He overtook Jason Witten for the second-most receiving yards by a TE in NFL history.

Swift can be seen going crazy for the play, as Kelce set up a Harrison Butker field goal that made it 24-10. Kelce finished with 3 catches on 5 targets for 71 yards in the win with no touchdowns.

He got limited targets as the Chiefs leaned heavily into their run game, with reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III dominating the offense.

With Kelce electing to play instead of retiring, this game was an efficient display of how the Chiefs can continue maximizing their veteran TE without being overly reliant on his production.

Can Travis Kelce become the all-time leader in receiving yards by a TE?

Kelce is now at 13,067 career receiving yards, passing Witten's old mark of 13,046, for No. 2 on the list. The legendary Tony Gonzalez ranks No. 1 with 15,127 yards.

With Kelce currently behind by over 2000 yards, it's not realistic to view him as someone who will break that record.

At his age and current production, Kelce would need at least three full seasons where he puts up over 700 yards to crack this record.

While Kelce has said he wants to play 'until the wheels fall off,' it's hard to imagine him playing until 2028 just to chase the record.

If he has a huge statistical season in 2026 or 2027, he might come back for 2028 to break the record, but a player as accomplished as him on and off the field is unlikely to feel that pressure.

With the Chiefs having an elite run game with Walker, and other catching targets like Xavier Worthy and Rashee Rice , it's hard to see how Kelce can have the volume or longevity necessary to break the record.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Talks 1st Game Back After Injury Rehab, Chiefs' Dominant Win vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes had a long road to recovery ahead of him after suffering a torn ACL last December, but the Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback attacked his rehab and managed to get back on the field by Week 1.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes had a long road to recovery ahead of him after suffering a torn ACL last December, but the Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback attacked his rehab and managed to get back on the field by Week 1.

His work came to fruition on Monday with a 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.

"I just wanted to play. I've done so much rehab, so much work to kind of put myself in this position," Mahomes said. "I just wanted to get out there and play. This is what you do it for, and I was able to play and go out there, and my guys around me kind of helped me."

Mahomes was far from the best version of himself as he threw for 184 yards and an interception on 15-of-27 passing, adding three total touchdowns. But he knew he'd need some time to get back into the swing of things, and he got tremendous support from his teammates.

"I didn't feel like I played my best football," Mahomes said. "We were still able to go out there and beat a really good football team pretty well cause the guys around me stepped up and knew that they were going to have to help me as I kinda of get back in the rhythm of things."

Mahomes' newest weapon stole the show as Kenneth Walker III accounted for 191 total yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes' familiar weapon, tight end Travis Kelce, picked up three receptions for 71 yards.

Mahomes will look to do a bit more next week against the Indianapolis Colts, but he was just thrilled to be back on the field.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni Makes NFL History After Eagles Win vs Commanders
articles.summary: Going into the 2026 NFL season opener for the Philadelphia Eagles, the head coach Nick Sirianni had a chance to land on a historical list. With a 24-22 Eagle...
articles.body:
Going into the 2026 NFL season opener for the Philadelphia Eagles , the head coach Nick Sirianni had a chance to land on a historical list.

With a 24-22 Eagles win over the Washington Commanders , Sirianni is making history.

According to the Eagles' Director of Football Communications, John Gonoude, there are five coaches in NFL history to win their first six career season openers. Sirianni is the latest to make the list.

In addition to Sirianni, the list includes Jim Harbaugh, Mike Shanahan, George Allen, and Potsy Clark.

George Allen is the lone Hall of Famer on the list, making it to Canton, Ohio, in 2002. He went on to have a 12-year NFL career.

Jim Harbaugh is the only coach on the list who is still active in the NFL. While he currently coaches the Los Angeles Chargers , Harbaugh started his NFL head coaching career with the San Francisco 49ers . After coaching them for four seasons, Harbaugh moved to college to coach at Michigan. He returned to the NFL in 2024.

The Eagles hired Sirianni in 2021. He was the replacement for Doug Pederson.

Sirianni first got his start in the NFL as an offensive quality control coach with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2009. He held a total of four positions with the Chiefs before going to the Chargers from 2013 to 2017. From 2018 to 2020, Sirianni coached the Indianapolis Colts as their offensive coordinator.

Since the Eagles hired Sirianni, they've been one of the most successful teams in the NFL. The head coach has never posted a losing season. The Eagles are two-time NFC Champions under Sirianni's management, and they won Super Bowl LIX in 2024.

With a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders, the Eagles start the 2026 run off with a 1-0 record, helping Sirianni improve his overall record to 60-26.

articles.body:
You know, college football can be odd. You can win two games decisively, covering the spread against FBS competition in the Ohio Bobcats (+23.5) and the Bowling Green Falcons (+30.5). The Nebraska Cornhuskers did that to open the 2026 campaign, beating the Former Fighting Frankies 49-21 on September 5 before routing the really bad Bowlers 56-7 this past Saturday.

But with the FCS division's North Dakota Fighting Hawks knocking on the Memorial Stadium door, the FanDuel Sportsbook is holding an early line as Nebraska at 24.5 point favorites.

(I kid, you played for the Titans, you've suffered enough.)

The Hawks are not to be overlooked. North Dakota is 3-0 on the season and can score. They haven't scored less than 42 points in a game and are averaging 50.3 ppg in 2026.

Yes, Nebraska is 2-0 and they are getting some attention from national eyes, receiving votes in the American Football Coaches Association. But the early schedule has been built to give the team confidence, to give us hope, and to drive ticket sales. But the Hawks are the sixth-ranked team in the FCS. Nebraska is the lone FBS school on NoDak's schedule before they hit the gauntlet of the Missouri Valley Conference, where they will face teams like South Dakota State (3), Illinois State (4), Youngstown State (9), South Dakota (12), and Southern Illinois University Carbondale (25). The MVC is the toughest overall conference in the FCS (damn Montana and Montana State standing in the way). In the Hawks' last game against FBS competition, they lost 38-35 at Kansas State.

This is the last tune-up before Big Ten play. For the Huskers, it's a chance to fix some mental errors and clean up their game before the trek to East Lansing. What does Dana Holgorsen have dialed up in this game? Will Rob Aurich's defense continue to minimize the damage? Will a number-one running back emerge, or will it continue to be RB by committee? And will the stable of wide receivers break loose for another big day?

It's a 6:15pm kickoff on Saturday. And you know you will be watching.

articles.title: ‘I Am Disgusted’ — Ex-NFL LB Gets Brutally Honest About Deshaun Watson, Claims It’s ‘Not Even Fair’ for Browns Fans To Watch $230M QB
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson waited nearly two years to make another NFL regular-season start after winning the Cleveland Browns’ starting quarterback job over Shedeur San...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson waited nearly two years to make another NFL regular-season start after winning the Cleveland Browns ' starting quarterback job over Shedeur Sanders . But his Week 1 performance drew sharp criticism from former player-turned NFL analyst Emmanuel Acho .

Watson's return ended in a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars , with Cleveland falling behind 31-0 before finally reaching the end zone late in the fourth quarter.

Emmanuel Acho Rips Deshaun Watson After Browns' Week 1 Loss

Acho did not soften his assessment of the $230 million quarterback's performance or what Browns fans had been forced to watch.

"I'm not just surprised. I am disgusted with how bad Deshaun played today," Acho said during a Speakeasy segment . "That was an aberration to the game of football."

Acho's frustration centered on basic quarterback play. He questioned why Watson was taking deep drops from shotgun, pointed to the interception on Cleveland's opening possession, and noted that the Browns nearly gave the ball away again on the next series.

"Deshaun, did y'all not practice together?" Acho asked. "Cleveland offense, did y'all not have any training camp? What the hell did we watch?"

The former NFL linebacker shifted his criticism toward what Cleveland's fan base has endured.

"You can't put Browns fans through that," Acho said, and added that rookie quarterbacks making their first career starts can look "more composed" than Watson did Sunday.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Shedeur Sanders Debate Is Already Back in Cleveland

Watson finished 16 of 22 for 205 yards, one touchdown, and one interception while taking five sacks. Forty-six of those passing yards came on a touchdown to Denzel Boston with 1:52 remaining after Jacksonville had already decided the game.

His current 64.5 grade in PFN's QB Impact Rating ranks him No. 27 among qualifying quarterbacks.

The ugly opener subsequently revived calls for Shedeur Sanders , who watched Week 1 from the sideline after losing the starting competition to Watson.

Watson's contract remains an unavoidable part of that debate. Cleveland gave him a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million deal in 2022, and his struggles since his arrival have made every poor performance harder for the organization to explain away.

Todd Monken is not changing quarterbacks yet. After reviewing the film on Monday, the Browns coach said he anticipates Watson starting in Week 2 against Tampa Bay and pointed to some positive plays he believes Cleveland can build on.

For now, Watson gets another start. For Browns fans, Acho argues that patience should not be unlimited because Cleveland once guaranteed him $230 million.

articles.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims made NFL history on ‘Monday Night Football’
articles.summary: Broncos WR Marvin Mims made NFL history during the team's loss to the Chiefs on Monday.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos Swiss Army Knife weapon Marvin Mims quietly made NFL history in the Broncos ' 31-10 loss at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday.

Mims didn't have to break a big punt return. All he had to do was not lose 98 yards. With two punt returns for 36 yards on Monday night, Mims hit the qualifying minimum number of punt returns required (75) to hold the NFL mark for the best yards-per-punt-return average in a career. Mims' career average surpassed 15.8, eclipsing New England Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones , who previously held the record of 14.3 yards-per-punt-return.

With Monday's stats in the books, Mims now has totaled 1,208 yards and scored one touchdown on 76 punt returns while adding 1,249 yards and another touchdown on 47 career kickoff returns. Mims also has 1,202 receiving yards and 150 rushing yards to his name, for a grand total of 3,809 all-purpose yards in just over three seasons of work.

Mims was selected in the second round of the 2023 NFL draft out of Oklahoma. Although Mims hasn't consistently been a full-time part of the offense, he has been a very effective returner, earning two Pro Bowl nods and All-Pro honors as a specialist in 2023 and 2024.

Mims is now in a contract year, and is looking to once again be a game-changer in the return game, and break into the offensive game plan as the Broncos move deeper into their 2026 schedule.
